items.text: MARYLANDERS: Open enrollment for marketplace health plans ends on January 15. You have more options to get affordable health care than ever before. Use https://t.co/6yvq9x29mo to comparison shop and pick the coverage that’s right for you. https://t.co/eG81HjMqv8

The health of our wastewater treatment plants is critical infrastructure that we cannot take for granted. I’m glad to join my colleagues to help upgrade the Grantsville treatment plant and provide safe, clean water access to Marylanders in Garrett County.
https://t.co/qJuDdEwXqc

The impact from these freezes are far reaching—from nutrition assistance to farm aid to highway funding to small business loans to workforce education to cancer and innovation research @NIST, @NIH. But, listen MD-06: I will have your back and work to defend this funding.

I also toured @HememicsI, a small business developing lab-quality testing for drug use, biotoxins & proteins via a handheld instrument for use in the field, which has applications in environmental safety, the military and in urgent care to better diagnose patients and save lives. https://t.co/TuxLLNGqjg

I am deeply concerned about the House Republicans’ reconciliation bill instructing the Energy and Commerce Committee, which has jurisdiction over Medicaid, to find $880 billion in savings over the next 10 years. To accomplish this mandate, heavy cuts to Medicaid coverage or federal cost share with states are expected—if not inevitable. My full statement below ⬇️

On National Nurses Day, I send thanks to nurses who show up every day for their patients … even when tired, stressed, and overworked.  You all are incredible!  Caring for others at their most vulnerable time is a vital community service and we commend your experience, patience, and kindness. #NationalNursesDay

Republicans are working to extend Trump’s tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans. To pay for it, they're cutting $300 billion from vital nutrition programs like SNAP, which helps 42 million Americans to put food on the table.

In our district, 1 in 9 families rely on SNAP—half of whom are children.

As Maryland's only voice on @HouseAgDems, I'll keep fighting these cruel cuts and push for a real bipartisan Farm Bill that supports our farmers and families.

Stay tuned. https://t.co/ealirESJ27

Today in our @HouseAgDems committee session, I expressed my concern that the Reconciliation bill eliminates SNAP-Ed. In Maryland alone, it supports more than 70 jobs and partners with over 600 organizations statewide. It reaches thousands - from school wellness policies to Pre-K nutrition. Cutting it is reckless. #SAVESNAPEd

I requested $3 million in federal funding to support the design and engineering of a critical expansion at GRMC’s Radiology/Oncology Department.

This pre-construction work is the first step toward a radiation treatment facility that will bring life-saving cancer care closer to home — especially for underserved and rural residents who often travel hours for treatment.

With rural hospitals facing increasing financial strain, targeted investments like this are vital to protect access to quality care where it’s needed most

I’ve been hearing from so many people across the aisle in my district—working parents, veterans, retirees—worried they’re about to lose their health coverage. And they’re right to be concerned. More than 175,000 Marylanders are at risk of being dropped from Medicaid under the new federal rollback.

Maryland deserves better. We all do.

Team McClain Delaney had the privilege of touring the @DaVita in Germantown and seeing firsthand the exceptional care provided to patients with kidney disease. Grateful for the dedication of the team pictured here—including the Director, Charge Nurse, Social Worker, and Dietitian—who go above and beyond every day to deliver lifesaving treatment and holistic support.

In Maryland’s 6th District, 1 in 3 kids rely on Medicaid. Thousands more rely on SNAP to get enough to eat.

We should never accept a country where a child goes hungry or without care. Our values demand better.

I’m fighting back against these cruel cuts—because our kids deserve a future we can be proud of.

Visiting The Arc of Washington County, Inc. reminded me of the incredible individuals they support and the life-changing impact of their programs. 

The recent Big Budget Bill, now law, includes Medicaid cuts that threaten this vital care—but I am fighting in Congress to lessen their impact and ultimately reverse them. This is about our values, and I strongly believe that everyone deserves the support to live with dignity and independence. 
https://t.co/z8kYtBsX88

Thank you to the seniors of @ActsRetirement in Adamstown for welcoming me recently.

I know these past months have been challenging. Recent cuts to the Social Security Administration, Medicaid, SNAP, and public broadcasting threaten programs that so many of you rely on to live with dignity, stay healthy and stay connected. But I will continue to fight to ensure our seniors have the care, resources and respect you deserve.

My office is here to help with questions about benefits, Medicare, VA support and more—you are never alone.

I’m honored to share that $1 million in my requested Community Project Funding has been approved in the next federal funding package to improve radiation oncology services at Garrett Regional Medical Center. These funds will help build a radiation treatment facility, bringing lifesaving care closer to home for families in Garrett County and surrounding areas.
Rural communities face higher cancer rates and far fewer treatment options. I won’t stand by while access to care is limited—together, we can ease the physical, financial and emotional burdens that come with this devastating disease.

At @UPMC and Garrett Regional Medical Center this week, I heard directly from doctors, nurses, and patients deeply concerned about the Big Budget Bill.

Medicaid cuts won’t just appear on paper—they’ll be felt in our communities, especially in Western Maryland, which is already a designated physician shortage area.

Health care should never be partisan. Every child, parent, and senior deserves quality care close to home. I’ll keep working with partners at every level to push back against these cuts and fight for the health of Western Maryland. https://t.co/0VdBiiz72p

Last week, I visited Garrett Regional Medical Center to discuss federal healthcare challenges with CEO Mark Boucot and the hospital leadership. GRMC serves over 46,000 Marylanders, many of whom rely on Medicaid, and one of my biggest priorities in Congress is to ensure that our rural hospitals have the resources they need to serve their local communities. 

Recent cuts to Medicaid and new adjustments to reimbursement formulas are of great concern to our health providers nationally, and I want to make sure Garrett County is continued to be blessed by GRMC and other local providers that serve their community with great heart and dedication. @mhaonline

Glad to sit down today with @GovWesMoore at the U.S. Capitol. As Team Maryland, we discussed @fema aid for Mountain Maryland, support for our farmers and rural areas, investments in infrastructure and pushing back against harmful cuts to Medicaid, SNAP and the vital services Marylanders rely on every day. 

Maryland, like every state, is facing some incredible challenges, but we are strong and united in purpose. Under Governor Moore’s exceptional leadership, we can meet this moment together to ensure that all our communities continue to thrive and that “no one is left behind.”

Last week, I sat down with some of our neighbors in Garrett County. What did they tell me? Our rural families have some real concerns: lack of affordable housing, educational resources stretched thin, Medicaid cuts, the need for more good-paying jobs and for more infrastructure investment. 

Over some hot @Traders_Coffee and freshly baked pastries, we discussed how our communities can come together to address these issues and the need to push back against the funding cuts from the federal to county levels. Your stories are an essential part of why I fight every day to have the backs of my constituents in Mountain Maryland. @GCCommissioners @GCMDEconDev

Half of all moms in rural America deliver their babies on Medicaid. For many families, it’s the only way to get prenatal care and a safe delivery.
https://t.co/5hk3S50oLC

But because of this reckless budget bill (now law), 32,000 Marylanders in our 6th District are projected to lose Medicaid over the next decade. That’s thousands of neighbors, parents and children who could be left without care.

I will not stop fighting to protect Medicaid and the dignity of every Maryland family.

Heading into the @HouseAgDems hearing on specialty crop insurance! From Butler's Orchard and Lewis Orchards to every other farm across Maryland, I’m fighting for the policies that help our farmers thrive. Every orchard, field, and family farm matters. 

As Maryland's only voice on the Ag Committee, I’m proud to bring their voices to Washington. @FarmBureauMD

At yesterday’s grand opening of Meritus Commons, it was my pleasure to present a certificate to the advocates who made it all possible. @MeritusHealth and their School of Osteopathic Medicine went above and beyond, bringing a new generation of healthcare professionals to Hagerstown and ensuring that those students have a designated, residential space to study and live. I cannot wait to see these future doctors grow and serve the patients they’ve dedicated their careers to helping.

No one wants a shutdown, but our country’s values and health are at stake. This week I met Tony Gonzales, a father diagnosed with cancer and now undergoing chemo. If current ACA tax credits are not included in this CR, he won’t be able to afford premiums, which are projected to nearly double. I remember my devastation when my dad passed from cancer. Health care costs are not just numbers, but impact real people with families and community. 

Tony’s story echoes the strength of so many in need of life-saving services — their healthcare is at stake in this critical moment, and this shutdown must be a turning point for Americans and for our values.  If we love America, we need to value and care for our fellow Americans.

Today I joined @GovWesMoore at Montgomery County Health Department’s Silver Spring Center, standing up to protect healthcare and cuts to Medicaid access and other critical services. Failure to extend ACA tax credits will impact the ability of our rural health providers to remain open and result in the almost doubling of health premiums for everyone. This is about our values and who we are as Americans, and I will not let our state and your needs be held hostage to partisanship, retribution and cruel hearted cuts. In Maryland, we leave no one behind.
